core_obligations: Prove (1) by induction on n, using the hypothesis to control Tor one against the quotients by powers of the ideal (proof lines 23882-23905).
Prove (2) by resolving a module annihilated by a power of the ideal through successive quotients and using the long exact Tor sequence, then specialise to nilpotent ideals (proof lines 23905-23932).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the power to get flatness modulo each power (proof lines 23881-23905).
Use the Tor sequence for modules killed by a power (proof lines 23905-23933).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if a module is flat modulo an ideal and Tor one against the quotient by that ideal vanishes, then the module is flat modulo every power and Tor one vanishes against every module annihilated by a power, hence the module is flat when the ideal is nilpotent (statement lines 23867-23879). The proof does not invoke the local criterion: it inducts on the exponent to get flatness modulo each power, and then resolves a module killed by a power through successive quotients, using the long exact Tor sequence (proof lines 23881-23933). Reducing the general module to modules killed by a single power is the step that carries the second part. H2.
